speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset lower back pain radiating down your leg; to determine the exact cause, I need to ask you a few questions. Can you tell me how many hours ago this pain started and what specific activity you were doing when it began?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your description of sharp pain radiating down the side of your leg and foot during exercise, could you describe the specific sensations you feel in your foot, such as numbness, tingling, or weakness? Additionally, does the pain worsen when you cough, sneeze, or bear down?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Lumbar_Spine - Findings: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: L5-S1 Lumbar Disc Herniation with Radiculopathy. The MRI confirms a herniated disc at the L5-S1 level impinging on the nerve root, which explains your sudden onset of sharp back pain radiating down the leg and foot following exertion.
